answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks via multiparty TLS proofs bound to aged external accounts. An agent executes a joint TLS session with an attestor to prove account tenure and emit a scoped nullifier, which a cedar policy verifier checks against a public mirror of spent tags. Because each identity consumes a scarce, seasoned account, attackers cannot cheaply clone agents across ferrous server racks. However, illicit brokers can still supply stolen or pre-farmed legacy accounts.
